summary: Analyses certified robustness of ensembles, proving diversified gradients and large confidence margins are necessary and sufficient under model smoothness, and proposes Diversity Regularized Training, which yields higher certified L2 robustness than single and ensemble models on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

title: On the Convergence of Certified Robust Training with Interval Bound Propagation
summary: Analyses convergence of Interval Bound Propagation certified training, proving that for an overparameterized two-layer ReLU network with logistic loss, gradient descent converges linearly to zero robust training error with high probability given small perturbation radius and large width.

title: Policy Smoothing for Provably Robust Reinforcement Learning
summary: Policy smoothing adds Gaussian noise to observations so the total reward of a reinforcement learning agent is certified against adaptive adversaries, based on an adaptive Neyman-Pearson lemma; tested on Cartpole, Pong, Freeway and Mountain Car.

title: Provably Robust Adversarial Examples
summary: Constructs provably robust adversarial examples, connected input regions certified to contain only adversarial inputs under pixel intensity or geometric perturbations, by iteratively refining sampled regions with volume-maximizing optimization until a verifier certifies them; PARADE finds regions with about 10^573 and 10^599 adversarial examples, and these regions are more effective against randomized smoothing defenses than the single attacks used to build them.

title: Sound and Complete Neural Network Repair with Minimality and Locality Guarantees
summary: REASSURE repairs ReLU networks by adding a patch network on the linear region of a buggy input, giving sound and complete repair that is minimal in function space and leaves outputs away from the repair region unchanged.

title: CC-CERT: A Probabilistic Approach to Certify General Robustness of Neural Networks
summary: CC-CERT gives probabilistic robustness certificates for neural networks under general attacks, including semantic transformations such as rotation and translation, by estimating failure probability under a sampled attack distribution with Chernoff-Cramer bounds.

title: DeformRS: Certifying Input Deformations with Randomized Smoothing
summary: DeformRS-VF and DeformRS-Par certify networks against vector-field and parameterized input deformations, such as rotations, translations, scaling and affine maps, via randomized smoothing; DeformRS-Par reaches 39% certified accuracy for rotations within 10 degrees on ImageNet.

title: Distillation of RL Policies with Formal Guarantees via Variational Abstraction of Markov Decision Processes
summary: Distills deep RL policies into discrete latent Markov decision process models learned by a variational autoencoder, with bisimulation bounds and PAC guarantees that let formal MDP methods check reachability, safety-constrained reachability and discounted-reward objectives.

title: GoTube: Scalable Statistical Verification of Continuous-Depth Models
summary: GoTube statistically verifies continuous-depth neural models by solving global optimization problems over time to build a reachable tube that is conservative up to chosen probability and tightness, avoiding the wrapping effect and outscaling existing reachability tools.

title: Input-Specific Robustness Certification for Randomized Smoothing
summary: Input-Specific Sampling speeds up randomized smoothing certification by adapting the sample size to each input while bounding the radius loss; it certifies over three times faster on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet at a cost of 0.05 certified radius.

title: Recurrent Neural Network Controllers Synthesis with Stability Guarantees for Partially Observed Systems
summary: Synthesizes recurrent neural network controllers for partially observed nonlinear uncertain systems with stability guarantees, using convex conditions from integral quadratic constraints and the S-lemma enforced by a projected policy gradient method that needs fewer samples.

title: Stability Verification in Stochastic Control Systems via Neural Network Supermartingales
summary: Verifies almost-sure asymptotic stability of nonlinear stochastic control systems with neural network policies by learning neural ranking supermartingales, which also give the first bounds on stabilization time; tested on stochastic reinforcement learning environments.

title: Tight Neural Network Verification via Semidefinite Relaxations and Linear Reformulations
summary: Tightens SDP-based neural network verification by adding linear cuts from the reformulation-linearisation technique to a layerwise SDP relaxation; on MNIST networks of about 10k nodes the share of certified cases rises from 0% to 82%.

title: Towards Automating Model Explanations with Certified Robustness Guarantees
summary: A concept-based interpretation method that automatically produces prototype-based concept explanations without human intervention and gives certified robustness guarantees that these explanations hold under adversarial perturbations, tested on real-world datasets.

title: Verification of Neural-Network Control Systems by Integrating Taylor Models and Zonotopes
summary: Verifies closed-loop neural-network control systems by chaining Taylor-model reachability for the dynamics with zonotope analysis for the network without losing dependency information; the tool is the first to analyse all benchmarks of an annual NNCS reachability competition.

title: A dual number abstraction for static analysis of Clarke Jacobians
summary: DeepJ soundly bounds the Clarke Jacobian of Lipschitz, possibly non-differentiable functions with an abstract domain over dual numbers and forward-mode dual interval evaluation, analysing Lipschitz robustness of networks under rotation, contrast, haze and composed perturbations.

title: Interval universal approximation for neural networks
summary: Proves an interval universal approximation theorem for networks with squashable activations, so provably robust l-infinity networks exist, but shows the needed range approximation problem is Delta-2-intermediate, so building such networks efficiently is inherently hard.

title: PRIMA: general and precise neural network certification via scalable convex hull approximations
summary: PRIMA verifies neural networks with any non-linear activation using multi-neuron convex abstractions from polynomial convex hull approximation algorithms; it verifies up to 20%, 30% and 34% more images on ReLU, Sigmoid and Tanh networks.

title: Beta-CROWN: Efficient Bound Propagation with Per-neuron Split Constraints for Neural Network Robustness Verification
summary: Encodes branch-and-bound neuron split constraints in bound propagation via optimizable β parameters, giving tighter bounds than LP verifiers at CROWN's GPU efficiency; with BaB it is up to three orders of magnitude faster than LP-based BaB, beats SDP verifiers with far less time, and powers α,β-CROWN, winner of VNN-COMP 2021.

title: Center Smoothing: Certified Robustness for Networks with Structured Outputs
summary: Center smoothing extends randomized smoothing to structured outputs such as sets, images and text, certifying that the output change, measured by a distance metric, stays small under any norm-bounded input perturbation, without much loss in base model performance.

title: Fast Certified Robust Training with Short Warmup
summary: Speeds up IBP certified training with a new weight initialization, full batch normalization and regularization against exploded bounds and ReLU imbalance, reaching 65.03% verified error on CIFAR-10 and 82.36% on TinyImageNet in 160 and 80 epochs.

title: Infinite Time Horizon Safety of Bayesian Neural Networks
summary: Verifies infinite-horizon safety of Bayesian neural network policies by training a separate deterministic certificate network, computing a safe weight set and rejecting posterior samples outside it; also extended to safe exploration in reinforcement learning.

title: Make Sure You're Unsure: A Framework for Verifying Probabilistic Specifications
Overcoming the Convex Barrier for Simplex Inputs
summary: Designs a tight convex relaxation for verifying robustness to perturbations within the probability simplex that stays linear in neuron count, improving l1 verified accuracy on CIFAR-10 and MNIST by up to 14.4% and verifying a multi-modal text-image classifier.

title: Partition-Based Formulations for Mixed-Integer Optimization of Trained ReLU Neural Networks
summary: Partition-based mixed-integer formulations of trained ReLU networks group node inputs and take convex hulls over partitions via disjunctive programming, trading size against tightness; the smaller relaxations outperform existing formulations in experiments.

title: Relaxing Local Robustness
summary: Introduces relaxed top-k robustness and affinity robustness, properties that allow some label sets to be close, and builds models that can be efficiently certified for them, giving lower rejection rates and higher certified accuracies than standard local robustness.

title: ScaleCert: Scalable Certified Defense against Adversarial Patches with Sparse Superficial Layers
summary: ScaleCert certifies defenses against adversarial patches on high-resolution images by using superficial important neurons for network compression, cutting adversarial region search and prediction noise; certified accuracy on ImageNet rises from 36.3% to 60.4%.

title: Semialgebraic Representation of Monotone Deep Equilibrium Models and Applications to Certification
summary: Gives a semialgebraic representation of ReLU monotone deep equilibrium models so semidefinite programming can certify robustness under general Lq norms, estimate Lipschitz constants and propagate ellipsoidal uncertainty, outperforming existing monDEQ certification.

title: SmoothMix: Training Confidence-calibrated Smoothed Classifiers for Certified Robustness
summary: SmoothMix trains smoothed classifiers on self-mixup combinations of samples along adversarial directions, calibrating confidence of over-confident near off-class samples, and markedly improves certified l2 robustness of randomized smoothing over existing robust training methods.

title: Towards Better Understanding of Training Certifiably Robust Models against Adversarial Examples
summary: Identifies smoothness of the loss landscape, besides bound tightness, as a key factor in certifiable training with linear relaxations, and designs a training method with both properties that performs well across a wide range of perturbation sizes.

title: Training Certifiably Robust Neural Networks with Efficient Local Lipschitz Bounds
summary: Trains certifiably robust networks with a tighter, trainable local Lipschitz bound that removes rows and columns for activations constant near each input, plus clipped activations with learnable thresholds; it improves clean and certified accuracy on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet.

title: Distribution Models for Falsification and Verification of DNNs
summary: DFV learns an input distribution model, prefixes it to the DNN and restates the property over its input space so existing falsifiers and verifiers target realistic inputs; a study with 7 tools and 93 models shows more representative counterexamples.

title: Cert-RNN: Towards Certifying the Robustness of Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Cert-RNN certifies robustness of recurrent networks such as vanilla RNNs and LSTMs with precise abstract transformers for their nonlinear operations, giving bounds on average 1.86 times larger than POPQORN on an MNIST sequence model.

title: DetectorGuard: Provably Securing Object Detectors against Localized Patch Hiding Attacks
summary: DetectorGuard provably secures object detectors against localized patch hiding attacks by checking objectness from a robust image classifier against detector boxes, so a certified object is detected or an alert is raised, at under 1% clean cost.

title: Learning Security Classifiers with Verified Global Robustness Properties
summary: Trains security classifiers, structured as ensembles of logic rules, to satisfy verified global robustness properties via a booster-fixer scheme using counterexample guided inductive synthesis; a Twitter spam classifier meets five properties with a 5.4% drop in true positive rate.

title: TSS: Transformation-Specific Smoothing for Robustness Certification
summary: TSS certifies robustness against semantic transformations, using transformation-specific randomized smoothing for resolvable ones like blur and stratified sampling for interpolating ones like rotation; it reaches 30.4% certified accuracy against rotations within 30 degrees on ImageNet.

title: Integer-arithmetic-only Certified Robustness for Quantized Neural Networks
summary: An integer randomized smoothing method with quantization gives smoothed classifiers that use only integer arithmetic, with a tight l2 robustness guarantee, matching accuracy and running 4 to 5 times faster than floating-point certified methods on CPUs and mobile devices.

title: Robustness Certification for Point Cloud Models
summary: 3DCertify verifies robustness of 3D point cloud models to semantic transformations using first-order Taylor relaxations for any differentiable transformation and a precise max-pool relaxation; it certifies 95.7% of point clouds against rotations of 60 degrees.

title: DEEPSPLIT: An Efficient Splitting Method for Neural Network Verification via Indirect Effect Analysis
summary: DeepSplit is a complete verifier for ReLU networks based on symbolic interval propagation that picks split nodes by their indirect effect on successor relaxations and encodes splits efficiently in linear programming, giving 1 to 2 orders of magnitude speedups.

title: Efficient Neural Network Verification via Layer-based Semidefinite Relaxations and Linear Cuts
summary: Verifies local robustness of neural networks with a layer-based semidefinite relaxation combined with linear cuts and chordal graph decompositions, provably tighter than prior approaches and an order of magnitude faster than earlier SDP methods.

title: On Guaranteed Optimal Robust Explanations for NLP Models
summary: Computes optimal robust explanations for NLP neural networks as word subsets that guarantee unchanged prediction under bounded embedding perturbations of the other words, using implicit hitting sets and maximum universal subsets, evaluated on SST, Twitter and IMDB.

title: Probabilistic Sufficient Explanations
summary: Defines probabilistic sufficient explanations, the simplest feature subsets that give strong probabilistic guarantees the classifier behaves the same under the data distribution, found with probabilistic circuits and expected predictions; compared favourably with Anchors and logical explanations.

title: Towards Scalable Complete Verification of Relu Neural Networks via Dependency-based Branching
summary: Complete verification of ReLU networks that branches on ReLU states according to dependencies between nodes, giving MILP sub-problems with fewer integer constraints; on the fully connected networks of the first verification competition it reports 145% gains over prior complete methods.

title: Verifying Reinforcement Learning up to Infinity
summary: Verifies time-unbounded safety of neural network controllers for dynamical systems with abstract interpretation that builds template polyhedra via MILP and interval arithmetic, yielding safe invariant overapproximations of the reach set for linear, piecewise linear and nonlinear dynamics.

title: PatchGuard: A Provably Robust Defense against Adversarial Patches via Small Receptive Fields and Masking
summary: PatchGuard provably defends image classifiers against localized adversarial patches by using CNNs with small receptive fields to bound corrupted features and a robust masking aggregation, with strong provable and clean accuracy on ImageNet, ImageNette and CIFAR-10.

title: CRFL: Certifiably Robust Federated Learning against Backdoor Attacks
summary: CRFL trains federated learning models with certified robustness against backdoors by clipping and smoothing model parameters, giving sample-wise certificates tied to poisoning ratio, attacker count and training iterations, and the first benchmark for this setting.

title: Explanations for Monotonic Classifiers
summary: Gives algorithms polynomial in classifier run time and feature count to compute one formal explanation of a black-box monotonic classifier, plus a practical model-agnostic algorithm for enumerating formal explanations.

title: Globally-Robust Neural Networks
summary: Builds globally-robust networks by integrating efficient global Lipschitz bounds into training, producing models certifiable by construction with low time and memory cost; a large Tiny-Imagenet model trains in hours, and local bounds are proved not to raise maximum verifiable accuracy.

title: Improved, Deterministic Smoothing for L1 Certified Robustness
Provable Lipschitz Certification for Generative Models
summary: Upper bounds the Lipschitz constant of generative models by approximating the set of vector-Jacobian products with layerwise zonotope abstractions, giving tight bounds on small networks and scaling to VAE and DCGAN architectures.

title: Scalable Certified Segmentation via Randomized Smoothing
summary: Certifies image and point cloud segmentation with randomized smoothing, using multiple-testing correction and allowing abstention on single pixels or points; achieves competitive accuracy with guarantees on Pascal Context, Cityscapes and ShapeNet.

title: Skew Orthogonal Convolutions
summary: Skew Orthogonal Convolution builds orthogonal, gradient-norm-preserving convolution layers from the exponential of a skew-symmetric Jacobian with a bounded Taylor approximation, training provably Lipschitz CNNs faster with better standard and certified accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

title: Towards Certifying L-infinity Robustness using Neural Networks with L-inf-dist Neurons
summary: Introduces l-infinity-dist neurons whose networks are 1-Lipschitz under the l-infinity norm, giving certified robustness from output margins; reaches 93.09% certified accuracy on MNIST, 35.42% on CIFAR-10 and 16.31% on TinyImageNet.

title: An Iterative Scheme of Safe Reinforcement Learning for Nonlinear Systems via Barrier Certificate Generation
summary: SRLBC synthesizes safe DNN controllers for nonlinear systems by alternating deep RL training with a verifier that computes a maximal safe initial region and barrier certificate via polynomial abstraction and bilinear matrix inequalities, handling systems up to dimension 12.

title: Automated Safety Verification of Programs Invoking Neural Networks
summary: Verifies system-level safety of programs that call neural networks by tightly integrating program analysis and network analysis in an abstract interpretation framework, evaluated on 26 variants of a restricted autonomous-driving benchmark.

title: BDD4BNN: A BDD-Based Quantitative Analysis Framework for Binarized Neural Networks
summary: BDD4BNN encodes binarized neural networks into Binary Decision Diagrams through cardinality constraints over blocks, enabling precise quantitative robustness analysis and interpretability of BNNs, with a prototype tool showing effectiveness and efficiency.

title: DNNV: A Framework for Deep Neural Network Verification
summary: DNNV standardizes input and output formats for DNN verifiers, offers a DSL for properties, and applies simplification and reduction operations so more verifiers can run existing benchmarks, raising benchmark support from 30% to 74%.

title: NNrepair: Constraint-Based Repair of Neural Network Classifiers
summary: NNrepair repairs neural network classifiers by fault localization followed by constraint solving to modify parameters at an intermediate or last layer; on MNIST and CIFAR-10 it improves accuracy by 45.56 points on poisoned and 10.40 on adversarial data.

title: PEREGRiNN: Penalized-Relaxation Greedy Neural Network Verifier
summary: PEREGRiNN verifies polytopic input-output specifications of ReLU networks using a convex solver both as feasibility checker and to penalize relaxation, pushing large relaxations toward the input; it verifies more properties faster on an MNIST robustness suite.

title: Robustness Verification of Semantic Segmentation Neural Networks Using Relaxed Reachability
summary: Verifies robustness of semantic segmentation networks in NNV via a relaxed reachability method that solves only a chosen share of LPs and supports up-sampling layers, measuring robust pixel percentage and robust IoU on M2NIST with reduced verification time.

title: Scalable Polyhedral Verification of Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Prover, a verifier for recurrent neural networks, computes polyhedral abstractions of nonlinear recurrent updates via sampling, optimization and Fermat's theorem, refining them by gradient descent; it certifies RNNs for vision, speech (with abstractions of the preprocessing pipeline) and motion-sensor classification beyond prior tools.

title: Verisig 2.0: Verification of Neural Network Controllers Using Taylor Model Preconditioning
summary: Verisig 2.0 checks closed-loop systems with tanh/sigmoid neural network controllers using Taylor-model reachability with preconditioning and shrink wrapping, parallelized for larger networks; on 10 benchmarks it is more accurate and faster than three tools, with speed-ups up to 21x and 268x.

title: Lyapunov-stable neural-network control
summary: Synthesizes a Lyapunov-stable neural-network controller together with a neural Lyapunov function, verifying the Lyapunov condition as a mixed-integer linear program that either certifies it or returns counterexamples; also inner-approximates the region of attraction, tested on pendulum and quadrotor robots.

title: Achieving Robustness in Classification Using Optimal Transport With Hinge Regularization
summary: Learns 1-Lipschitz binary and multi-class classifiers with a hinge-regularized Kantorovich-Rubinstein loss grounded in optimal transport, which yields a certifiable robustness bound; experiments show the guarantees hold without significant accuracy loss, and adversarial examples become visually meaningful.

title: PointGuard: Provably Robust 3D Point Cloud Classification
summary: PointGuard certifies 3D point cloud classifiers against adversarially modified, added or deleted points by majority voting over random point subsamples; the derived bound on the number of tolerated points is proven tight, with evaluation on ModelNet40 and ScanNet.

title: Simpler Certified Radius Maximization by Propagating Covariances
summary: Maximizes the certified radius of smoothed classifiers by propagating the covariance of the Gaussian smoothing distribution through the network instead of Monte Carlo sampling, giving runtime savings on moderately deep networks for CIFAR-10, ImageNet and Places365 at a small accuracy cost.

title: Towards Evaluating and Training Verifiably Robust Neural Networks
summary: Proves CROWN is always tighter than interval bound propagation with suitable bounding lines, proposes linear bound propagation (LBP) to verify large networks with lower verified error, and a ParamRamp activation that improves verified robustness on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet.

title: Fast and precise certification of transformers
summary: DeepT certifies Transformer networks via abstract interpretation with a Multi-norm Zonotope domain covering ℓ1 and ℓ2 perturbations, including transformers for softmax and dot product; it certifies radii 28x larger than prior work and handles synonym attacks on long word sequences.

title: Provable repair of deep neural networks
summary: Repairs a DNN so it provably satisfies a specification: Provable Point Repair finds minimal repairs for finite point sets with any activation, and Provable Polytope Repair handles convex polytopes for piecewise-linear networks, both reduced to linear programming via a Decoupled DNN architecture.

title: Robustness certification with generative models
summary: GenProve certifies classifiers against semantic image transformations produced by generative models, such as changing age or hair colour, by capturing infinite non-convex sets of activations and distributions over them, giving sound deterministic and probabilistic guarantees on realistic networks.

title: Certify or Predict: Boosting Certified Robustness with Compositional Architectures
summary: Boosts certified robustness without retraining by pairing an accurate deep network with a smaller certified network and adaptively selecting which one processes each input; on CIFAR-10 at ℓ∞ 2/255 it reaches 90.1% natural accuracy with 27.5% certified robustness.

title: Collective Robustness Certificates: Exploiting Interdependence in Graph Neural Networks
summary: Collective robustness certificates for Graph Neural Networks count how many predictions stay stable under a single shared perturbation, fusing single-node certificates using locality; on Citeseer node classification the average number of certifiable feature perturbations rises from 7 to 351.

title: Deep Partition Aggregation: Provable Defenses against General Poisoning Attacks
Efficient Certified Defenses Against Patch Attacks on Image Classifiers
summary: BagCert combines a model architecture with a certification procedure for adversarial patches, plus a loss for end-to-end training of certified patch robustness; on CIFAR10 it certifies 10,000 examples in 43 seconds on one GPU, with 86% clean and 60% certified accuracy against 5x5 patches.

title: Enforcing robust control guarantees within neural network policies
summary: Builds neural-network control policies that enforce the same provable robustness criteria as robust control by embedding convex-optimization-based projection layers, improving average-case performance over robust control and worst-case stability over non-robust deep RL on several domains.

title: Estimating Lipschitz constants of monotone deep equilibrium models
summary: Bounds the Lipschitz constants of monotone deep equilibrium models as a simple function of the strong monotonicity parameter, for both input-output and weight-output maps; the bounds are small relative to standard DNNs and yield depth-independent PAC-Bayes generalization bounds.

title: Fantastic Four: Differentiable and Efficient Bounds on Singular Values of Convolution Layers
summary: Derives four provable, differentiable upper bounds on the spectral norm of 2D multi-channel convolution layers and takes their minimum as an efficient bound usable to bound Lipschitz constants or curvature; as a regularizer it improves generalization and robustness on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

title: Fast and Complete: Enabling Complete Neural Network Verification with Rapid and Massively Parallel Incomplete Verifiers
summary: Replaces linear programming in branch-and-bound complete verification with backward-mode LiRPA on GPUs, adding gradient-based bound tightening, batch splits and minimal LP use to keep completeness; on a single GPU it runs an order of magnitude faster than LP-based approaches.

title: Fast Geometric Projections for Local Robustness Certification
summary: Checks ℓ2 local robustness of piecewise-linear feed-forward networks by searching for decision boundaries in nearby linear regions using simple geometric projections, implemented in parallel on GPU; it is more precise than many approximate verifiers and orders of magnitude faster than complete ones.

title: Fooling a Complete Neural Network Verifier
summary: Shows floating-point roundoff can be exploited to build adversarial networks whose true robustness differs sharply from what a complete verifier reports, and to plant backdoors the verifier misses; a small weight perturbation is offered as a simple defense against this attack.

title: Orthogonalizing Convolutional Layers with the Cayley Transform
summary: Parameterizes orthogonal convolutional layers by applying the Cayley transform to skew-symmetric convolutions in the Fourier domain; networks with these layers outperform prior deterministic certified defenses against ℓ2-bounded adversaries while scaling to larger architectures.

title: Provably robust classification of adversarial examples with detection
summary: Jointly trains a provably robust classifier and detector by adding an abstain/detection class and extending interval bound propagation to this objective under ℓ∞ perturbations; it outperforms plain IBP on MNIST and CIFAR-10, especially for large perturbations such as 8/255 and 16/255.

title: Scaling Symbolic Methods using Gradients for Neural Model Explanation
summary: Scales SMT-based analysis to large networks for model explanation by using Integrated Gradients to select first-layer neurons, then solving for minimal input masks that keep those activations above a threshold; resulting saliency maps on MNIST, ImageNet and Beer Reviews are sparser with higher saliency scores.

title: Scaling the Convex Barrier with Active Sets
summary: A dual algorithm operating on a small active set of dual variables makes a tighter, exponentially sized linear relaxation of piecewise-linear activations practical, with GPU parallelism and anytime valid bounds; it gives better bounds than off-the-shelf solvers in a fraction of their time.

title: Scalable Quantitative Verification For Deep Neural Networks
summary: PROVERO, a quantitative verification framework for deep neural networks, runs tests until a probabilistic property is proven with formal guarantees, for deterministic or randomized DNNs; applied to adversarial robustness, it certifies large DNNs where existing verifiers are inconclusive, needing only black-box access.

title: Efficient Reachability Analysis of Closed-Loop Systems with Neural Network Controllers
summary: Computes forward reachable sets of closed-loop systems with neural network controllers through a linear programming formulation with input set partitioning and support for measurement and process noise; it gives 10x less conservatism in half the computation time of prior methods, shown on a quadrotor.

title: Reachable Polyhedral Marching (RPM): A Safety Verification Algorithm for Robotic Systems with Deep Neural Network Components
summary: Reachable Polyhedral Marching computes exact forward and backward reachable sets of ReLU networks over multiple steps by incrementally enumerating polyhedral input cells, with early exit on unsafe cells; on ACAS Xu it finds unsafe actions many times faster than the fastest existing method.

title: Adaptive Verifiable Training Using Pairwise Class Similarity
summary: Improves verifiable training by clustering similar classes and assigning robustness criteria by inter-cluster similarity, via an Inter-Group Robustness Prioritization loss or a neural decision tree of sub-classifiers; clean performance improves up to 9.63% on Fashion-MNIST and 30.89% on CIFAR10.

title: Adversarial Training and Provable Robustness: A Tale of Two Objectives
summary: Trains certifiably robust networks by jointly optimizing empirical (adversarial) and provable robustness objectives with a gradient-descent technique that removes bias in stochastic multi-gradients, with convergence analysis; it matches or beats prior work on ℓ∞ robustness, reaching 6.60% verified error on MNIST at ε=0.3 and 66.57% on CIFAR-10 at ε=8/255.

title: Efficient Certification of Spatial Robustness
summary: Certifies robustness of vision models against vector field (spatial) transformations for the first time via model-agnostic convex relaxations that can be plugged into many neural network verifiers; experiments across architectures and datasets show effectiveness and scalability.

title: Fast Training of Provably Robust Neural Networks by SingleProp
summary: SingleProp is a regularizer for training provably robust networks that needs only one extra forward propagation, making it cheaper than certified defenses that run certification during training; on MNIST and CIFAR-10 it trains faster with comparable certified accuracy.

title: Intrinsic Certified Robustness of Bagging against Data Poisoning Attacks
summary: Proves that bagging with any base learner predicts the same label when the number of modified, deleted or inserted training examples stays below a threshold, which is tight without assumptions on the learner; on MNIST it reaches 91.1% certified accuracy against 100 arbitrarily changed training examples.

title: On Lipschitz Regularization of Convolutional Layers using Toeplitz Matrix Theory
summary: Uses Toeplitz matrix theory to derive an upper bound on the Lipschitz constant of convolutional layers that is both tight and cheap to compute, and builds on it an algorithm for training Lipschitz-regularized convolutional neural networks.

title: On the Verification of Neural ODEs with Stochastic Guarantees
summary: Verifies Neural ODEs with Stochastic Lagrangian Reachability, which builds a tight Reachtube using global optimization and gives confidence intervals on its bounds, avoiding the wrapping effect; a forward-mode adjoint sensitivity method speeds up gradients, and convergence rates are established.

title: Provably Secure Federated Learning against Malicious Clients
summary: Makes federated learning provably secure against malicious clients by training multiple global models on random client subsets and taking a majority vote, with a tight bound on tolerated malicious clients; it reaches 88% certified accuracy on MNIST with 20 of 1,000 clients malicious.

title: Scalable Verification of Quantized Neural Networks
summary: Shows that bit-exact verification of quantized neural networks with bit-vector specifications is PSPACE-hard, and proposes three techniques to scale SMT-based verification of such networks, giving speed-ups of up to three orders of magnitude over existing approaches.

title: Tightening Robustness Verification of Convolutional Neural Networks with Fine-Grained Linear Approximation
summary: DeepCert tightens robustness verification of convolutional networks with sigmoid-like activations through finer-grained linear approximations; on LeNet and MNIST/CIFAR models it improves the certified lower bound by up to 286.28% and runs up to 1566.76 times faster than other verifiers.

title: (De)Randomized Smoothing for Certifiable Defense against Patch Attacks
summary: Certifies image classifiers against adversarial patches with a de-randomized smoothing scheme that yields deterministic certificates and trains faster than interval-bound methods; for 5x5 patches on CIFAR-10 it reaches about 57.6% certified accuracy versus at most 30.3% before, and scales to ImageNet.

title: An efficient nonconvex reformulation of stagewise convex optimization problems
summary: Reformulates stagewise convex problems, including neural network verification, as nonconvex problems with simple bound constraints solved by a modified projected gradient method that reaches the global optimum; it yields small duality gaps quickly and outpaces off-the-shelf and specialized verification solvers.

title: Automatic Perturbation Analysis for Scalable Certified Robustness and Beyond
summary: Generalizes LiRPA bounds such as CROWN to arbitrary computational graphs in an automatic, differentiable framework with loss fusion, enabling certified defense on DenseNet, ResNeXt and Transformer and, for the first time, on Tiny ImageNet and Downscaled ImageNet; released as the auto_LiRPA library.

title: Black-Box Certification with Randomized Smoothing: A Functional Optimization Based Framework
summary: Casts randomized smoothing certification as functional optimization, allowing non-Gaussian smoothing distributions and attacks beyond ℓ2, including ℓ1 and ℓ∞; the framework exposes an accuracy-robustness trade-off, and its new distributions certify better than previous works.

title: Certifiably Adversarially Robust Detection of Out-of-Distribution Data
summary: Certifies worst-case out-of-distribution detection by using interval bound propagation to upper-bound classifier confidence over an ℓ∞-ball around OOD points and minimizing that bound in training; the guarantees generalize beyond the training OOD data with little accuracy loss.

title: Certified Defense to Image Transformations via Randomized Smoothing
Certified Monotonic Neural Networks
summary: Certifies monotonicity of general piecewise-linear neural networks with respect to chosen features by solving a mixed integer linear program, enabling training with increasing monotonicity regularization until certified; it is more accurate and efficient than methods like Deep Lattice Networks.

title: Certified Robustness of Graph Convolution Networks for Graph Classification under Topological Attacks
summary: Gives the first robustness certificate for graph convolution networks in graph classification under topological perturbations with local and global budgets, using Lagrange dualization and convex envelopes computed by dynamic programming; with robust training, more graphs are certified robust.

title: Certifying Confidence via Randomized Smoothing
summary: Certifies the prediction confidence of smoothed classifiers, as average score or margin, by modifying the Neyman-Pearson lemma to compute radii within which confidence stays above a threshold; using the confidence distribution gives notably larger certified radii on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

title: Certifying Strategyproof Auction Networks
summary: Verifies strategyproofness of RegretNet learned auction mechanisms under a given valuation profile with neural network verification techniques, modifying the architecture so it can be encoded exactly as an integer program, and produces certificates even where optimal mechanisms are unknown.

title: Consistency Regularization for Certified Robustness of Smoothed Classifiers
summary: Improves certified ℓ2 robustness of randomized-smoothing classifiers by regularizing prediction consistency over Gaussian noise during training, giving results better than or comparable to prior methods across architectures and datasets with less training cost and fewer hyperparameters.

title: Counterexample-Guided Learning of Monotonic Neural Networks
summary: COMET provably enforces monotonicity constraints on general ReLU networks at prediction time through counterexample-guided techniques, and uses monotonicity counterexamples as an inductive bias during training; on real-world datasets it outperforms existing monotonic learners.

title: Denoised Smoothing: A Provable Defense for Pretrained Classifiers
summary: Denoised smoothing makes any pretrained image classifier provably ℓp-robust by prepending a custom-trained denoiser and applying randomized smoothing, without modifying the classifier, in white-box and black-box settings; demonstrated on ImageNet, CIFAR-10 and the Azure, Google, AWS and ClarifAI APIs.

title: Detection as Regression: Certified Object Detection with Median Smoothing
Efficient Exact Verification of Binarized Neural Networks
summary: EEV performs exact verification of binarized neural networks with a SAT solver that natively handles reified cardinality constraints, plus training for solver-friendly BNNs; it gives exact ℓ∞ robustness results on convolutional BNNs for MNIST and CIFAR10, hundreds to thousands of times faster than real-valued verification.

title: Enabling certification of verification-agnostic networks via memory-efficient semidefinite programming
summary: A first-order dual SDP algorithm with memory linear in network activations, using iterative eigenvector methods via forward/backward passes on GPUs/TPUs, verifies networks not trained for verification; verified ℓ∞ accuracy rises from 1% to 88% on MNIST and 6% to 40% on CIFAR-10.

title: Exactly Computing the Local Lipschitz Constant of ReLU Networks
summary: Relates the local Lipschitz constant of nonsmooth functions to the generalized Jacobian, proves strong inapproximability for ReLU networks, and gives an algorithm computing the local Lipschitz constant exactly, used to assess the tightness of other Lipschitz estimators and the effects of regularized training.

title: Higher-Order Certification For Randomized Smoothing
summary: Extends randomized smoothing certification by framing radius computation as nested optimization and using first-order and higher-order information of Gaussian-smoothed classifiers, certifying larger safety regions with gains on ℓ1 radii and color-space ℓ2 radii on CIFAR10 and ImageNet.

title: Learning Certified Individually Fair Representations
summary: Learns representations certified for individual fairness: similar individuals are mapped within a certified ℓ∞ distance in latent space, so data consumers can certify fairness by proving ε-robustness of their classifier; evaluated on five real-world datasets with several fairness constraints.

title: Lipschitz Bounds and Provably Robust Training by Laplacian Smoothing
summary: Trains models with provable adversarial robustness by framing learning as Lipschitz-constrained loss minimization whose Lagrangian saddle point solves a weighted Laplacian Poisson equation, solved by graph discretization and primal-dual updates; also shows a fundamental robustness-accuracy lower bound.

title: Lipschitz-Certifiable Training with a Tight Outer Bound
summary: Speeds up certifiable training with box constraint propagation (BCP), combining Lipschitz analysis and interval arithmetic for a tighter outer bound; it trains over 12 times faster than a dual relaxation method with comparable verification and reaches 20.1% verified accuracy on Tiny ImageNet (ℓ2, 36/255).

title: Neurosymbolic Reinforcement Learning with Formally Verified Exploration
summary: Revel enables provably safe exploration in reinforcement learning by mirror descent between a neurosymbolic policy class and a verifiable symbolic class, avoiding repeated verification of neural networks; it enforces safe exploration where Constrained Policy Optimization fails and finds better policies.

title: On the Tightness of Semidefinite Relaxations for Certifying Robustness to Adversarial Examples
summary: Gives a geometric test of when the SDP relaxation certificate for ReLU network robustness is exact, viewing it as projecting a point onto a hyperbola; the certificate is proven exact for one hidden layer under mild assumptions and explained as usually conservative for several layers.

title: Semialgebraic Optimization for Lipschitz Constants of ReLU Networks
summary: Estimates global and local Lipschitz constants of multi-layer ReLU networks with a semidefinite programming hierarchy combining polynomial lifting of ReLU derivatives with a weak Putinar positivity certificate, sometimes giving better bounds in less time than linear programming approaches.

title: The Convex Relaxation Barrier, Revisited: Tightened Single-Neuron Relaxations for Neural Network Verification
summary: Derives the tightest convex relaxation of a ReLU over a box-bounded multivariate pre-activation input, separable in linear time, and builds LP-based and fast propagation verifiers on it that verify significantly more instances for a modest extra cost.

title: Perfectly parallel fairness certification of neural networks
summary: Libra certifies fairness of feed-forward neural networks for tabular classification with a perfectly parallel, sound static analysis; when certification fails it describes and quantifies biased input regions, with configurable scalability and precision for pay-as-you-go certification.

title: Practical Verification of Neural Network Enabled State Estimation System for Robotics
summary: Verifies robustness of learning-enabled robot state estimation, where a neural network feeds a Bayes filter, by reducing it to labelled transition systems with payoffs and solving a constrained optimization; on a Kalman-filter WAMI vehicle tracking system it verifies robustness and finds counterexamples.

title: NEURODIFF: Scalable Differential Verification of Neural Networks using Fine-Grained Approximation
summary: NeuroDiff verifies equivalence of two similar feed-forward ReLU networks, such as an original and compressed model, using new convex approximations of their difference plus selective symbolic variables; it is up to 1000x faster and 5x more accurate than the prior tool.

title: On Training Robust PDF Malware Classifiers
summary: Trains PDF malware classifiers with formally verified robustness properties over subtree insertions and deletions using verifiably robust training, achieving 92.27% average verified robust accuracy with 99.74% accuracy and 0.56% false positives, and raising evasion cost for unrestricted attackers.

title: Black-box Certification and Learning under Adversarial Perturbations
summary: Studies learning and third-party black-box certification of classifiers under adversarial perturbations in a PAC-type semi-supervised framework, giving possibility and impossibility results for VC-classes and analysing certification with a limited query budget.

title: Certified Robustness to Label-Flipping Attacks via Randomized Smoothing
summary: Uses randomized smoothing over arbitrary functions to certify classifiers against data poisoning, instantiated as linear classifiers certified against label flipping per test point with a deterministic analytical bound, little extra runtime, and the first multi-class label-flipping certificate.

title: Curse of Dimensionality on Randomized Smoothing for Certifiable Robustness
summary: Proves that for many i.i.d. smoothing distributions the largest certifiable ℓp radius shrinks with input dimension for p > 2, so Gaussian smoothing is optimal up to a constant factor; uniform ℓ1 and ℓ∞ smoothing scale even worse, with CIFAR experiments.

title: Efficient Robustness Certificates for Discrete Data: Sparsity-Aware Randomized Smoothing for Graphs, Images and More
summary: A sparsity-aware randomized smoothing certificate for discrete data that is model-agnostic, tight and efficient, with cost independent of input dimension or category count; it certifies any Graph Neural Network against perturbations to graph structure and node attributes.

title: Hierarchical Verification for Adversarial Robustness
summary: LayerCert performs exact ℓp robustness verification of ReLU networks by exploring activation regions hierarchically along the nested hyperplane arrangement induced by layers, provably solving fewer and smaller convex programs than GeoCert and reducing running time.

title: Neural Network Control Policy Verification With Persistent Adversarial Perturbation
Randomized Smoothing of All Shapes and Sizes
summary: A general theory for randomized smoothing finds optimal smoothing distributions via the Wulff Crystal and two methods for robust radii of any distribution, improving certified ℓ1 accuracy; Banach space cotypes show limits on certifying ℓp perturbations in high dimensions.

title: Robustness to Programmable String Transformations via Augmented Abstract Training
summary: Trains NLP models robust to user-defined string transformations such as insertions, deletions, substitutions and swaps, specified in a programmable language, by splitting specifications into parts handled by search and by abstraction; evaluated on AG and SST2.

title: Scalable Differential Privacy with Certified Robustness in Adversarial Learning
summary: Preserves differential privacy in adversarial learning for deep neural networks while certifying robustness, by randomizing input and latent spaces, an adversarial objective based on DP post-processing, and stochastic batch training that scales to large networks and datasets.

title: Second-Order Provable Defenses against Adversarial Attacks
summary: Computes ℓ2 robustness certificates for networks with differentiable activations via convex optimization when Hessian eigenvalues are bounded, using a differentiable curvature bound also as a regularizer; CRT reaches 69.79%, 57.78% and 53.19% certified accuracy on MNIST versus about 45% for IBP.

title: An Abstraction-Based Framework for Neural Network Verification
summary: Shrinks neural networks by over-approximation so properties proven on the smaller abstract network hold for the original, refining with counterexample guidance on spurious results; integrated with Marabou, it significantly improves verification performance on larger networks.

title: Improved Geometric Path Enumeration for Verifying ReLU Neural Networks
summary: Speeds up exact geometric path enumeration verification of ReLU networks through a series of optimizations, several algorithmically new, running sometimes hundreds of times faster on ACAS Xu and often fastest on harder instances, even beating over-approximating methods.

title: NNV: The Neural Network Verification Tool for Deep Neural Networks and Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems
summary: NNV is a set-based verification tool for deep neural networks and learning-enabled cyber-physical systems, using polyhedra, star sets, zonotopes and abstract domains for exact and over-approximate reachability, with closed-loop analysis via CORA; case studies cover ACAS Xu and adaptive cruise control.

title: Systematic Generation of Diverse Benchmarks for DNN Verification
summary: GDVB generates diverse neural network verification benchmarks by systematically varying problem factors that affect verifier performance, offering richer and less biased sets of verification problems for comparing verifiers.

title: Verification of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks Using ImageStars
summary: Verifies robustness of large CNNs such as VGG16 and VGG19 on ImageNet with the ImageStar set representation, combining concrete image operations with linear programming for exact and over-approximate analysis in NNV; it is less conservative and faster than zonotope and polytope methods.

title: Individual Fairness Revisited: Transferring Techniques from Adversarial Robustness
summary: Finds, for a given model, a metric under which it is individually fair: introduces minimal metrics and characterizes model behavior with them, then applies randomized smoothing to make complex models individually fair under a weighted Lᵖ metric, giving interpretable fairness guarantees at little utility cost.

title: Metamorphic Testing and Certified Mitigation of Fairness Violations in NLP Models
summary: Tests NLP models for fairness violations with metamorphic testing, then defines (ε, k)-fairness and smooths predictions to give certified fairness guarantees. Flags thousands of discriminatory inputs in popular commercial NLP models and adds certification at modest cost.

title: Verifiable RNN-Based Policies for POMDPs Under Temporal Logic Constraints
summary: Extracts a finite-state controller from an RNN policy for POMDPs with an iterative quantized bottleneck insertion, verifies it against temporal logic specifications with formal tools, and uses verification diagnostics to adjust memory or retrain the RNN; it beats traditional POMDP synthesis by 3 orders of magnitude while staying within 2% of optimal values.

title: Robustness Guarantees for Deep Neural Networks on Videos
summary: Bounds the maximum safe radius of CNN-RNN video classifiers over optical flow perturbations, using Lipschitz-based discretisation and a cooperative two-player game solved anytime, with gradient search for upper bounds and admissible A* for lower bounds; evaluated on UCF101.

title: Towards Verifying Robustness of Neural Networks Against A Family of Semantic Perturbations
summary: Semantify-NN verifies robustness to semantic perturbations such as hue, saturation, brightness, contrast and rotation by prepending semantic perturbation layers, so any ℓp-norm verifier applies; a refinement step tightens certificates beyond naive ℓp conversion across architectures and datasets.

title: ReluDiff: differential verification of deep neural networks
summary: ReluDiff performs differential verification of two closely related networks, such as an original and its compressed version, using a forward interval pass that exploits their similarity and gradient-guided backward refinement, giving orders-of-magnitude speedups and more proved properties.

title: A Framework for robustness Certification of Smoothed Classifiers using F-Divergences
summary: Generalises randomized smoothing to arbitrary smoothing measures and perturbation classes, certifying robustness of black-box smoothed classifiers via f-divergences; reports state-of-the-art certified robustness on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet and Librispeech audio classification.

title: Adversarial Training and Provable Defenses: Bridging the Gap
summary: COLT, convex layerwise adversarial training, trains certifiably robust networks by having an adversary search inside the verifier's convex relaxation at each layer. Reaches 60.5% certified robustness and 78.4% accuracy on CIFAR-10 at 2/255 L∞, beating concurrent results.

title: Certified Defenses for Adversarial Patches
summary: Shows existing preprocessing defenses against adversarial patches break under simple white-box attacks, then gives the first certified defense against patch attacks with faster training methods, reporting good robustness transfer across patch shapes and preliminary results for sparse attacks.

title: Certified Robustness for Top-k Predictions against Adversarial Perturbations via Randomized Smoothing
summary: Extends randomized smoothing certificates from top-1 to top-k predictions, deriving a tight ℓ2 robustness radius under Gaussian noise. On ImageNet it reaches 62.8% certified top-5 accuracy for perturbations with ℓ2 norm below 0.5; also evaluated on CIFAR10.

title: In Search for a SAT-friendly Binarized Neural Network Architecture
summary: Studies how binarized neural network architecture and training choices affect SAT-based reasoning, and proposes changes that yield SAT-friendly BNNs without accuracy loss, scaling existential and probabilistic queries to larger networks with significant speedups on all tested datasets.

title: Lipschitz constant estimation of Neural Networks via sparse polynomial optimization
summary: LiPopt computes increasingly tight upper bounds on neural network Lipschitz constants via polynomial optimization reduced to LP or SDP, exploiting sparse connectivity for convolutional and pruned networks; gives better ℓ∞-Lipschitz estimates than baselines on random and MNIST networks.

title: MACER: Attack-free and Scalable Robust Training via Maximizing Certified Radius
summary: MACER trains provably robust smoothed classifiers by directly maximizing the certified ℓ2 radius from randomized smoothing, without adversarial attacks. On CIFAR-10, ImageNet, MNIST and SVHN it trains faster than adversarial training and achieves larger average certified radius.

title: Neural Network Branching for Neural Network Verification
summary: Learns a branching strategy for branch-and-bound neural network verification with a graph neural network that imitates strong branching on the verified network's graph, roughly halving branches and verification time on convolutional networks and transferring to harder properties and larger networks.

title: Provable robustness against all adversarial $l_p$-perturbations for $p\geq 1$
Robustness Verification for Transformers
summary: The first robustness verification algorithm for Transformers, handling the cross-nonlinearity and cross-position dependency of self-attention layers. Its certified bounds are much tighter than naive Interval Bound Propagation and reflect word importance in sentiment analysis.

title: Towards neural networks that provably know when they don't know
Towards Stable and Efficient Training of Verifiably Robust Neural Networks
summary: CROWN-IBP trains verifiably robust networks by combining fast IBP bounds in a forward pass with tight CROWN linear-relaxation bounds in a backward pass, reaching 7.02% verified error on MNIST at ε=0.3 and 66.94% on CIFAR-10 at ε=8/255.

title: Towards Verified Robustness under Text Deletion Interventions
summary: Formally verifies that decomposable-attention natural language inference models do not grow more confident when arbitrary word subsets are deleted, using interval bound propagation. IBP training raises verified samples on SNLI from 2.8% to 18.4%.

title: Universal Approximation with Certified Networks
summary: Proves a universal approximation theorem for interval-certified ReLU networks: any continuous function can be approximated by a network whose interval bound propagation over a region is arbitrarily close to the function's optimal output range there.

title: Efficient Verification of ReLU-Based Neural Networks via Dependency Analysis
summary: Venus verifies ReLU feed-forward networks by exploiting dependency relations between ReLU nodes to prune the MILP search tree, combined with input domain splitting and symbolic interval propagation; evaluated on ACAS collision-avoidance, MNIST and CIFAR-10 models with considerable gains.

title: Fastened CROWN: Tightened Neural Network Robustness Certificates
summary: Proves that CROWN's solution is optimal for a given linear program under mild constraints, making costly LP-based certification unnecessary, and proposes FROWN, an optimization-based algorithm that tightens CROWN robustness certificates to certify larger robust regions across various networks.

title: Regularized Training and Tight Certification for Randomized Smoothed Classifier with Provable Robustness
summary: Trains base classifiers for Gaussian randomized smoothing with a regularized risk that adaptively encourages accuracy and robustness of the smoothed classifier, usable with standard or adversarial training, plus a certification algorithm that exploits the regularization for tighter high-probability ℓ2 robustness bounds on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

title: Robustness Certificates for Sparse Adversarial Attacks by Randomized Ablation
summary: Extends randomized smoothing to the ℓ0 threat model by randomly ablating input features instead of adding noise, certifying over 50% of MNIST images against any 8-pixel distortion and doubling or better the median certificates of a noise-based approach (8 vs 4 pixels on MNIST, 16 vs 1 on ImageNet).

title: Towards Certificated Model Robustness Against Weight Perturbations
summary: Certifies robustness of neural networks to weight perturbations by computing a bound within which outputs cannot be adversarially changed, and links this to weight quantization, yielding a robustness-aware quantization scheme that improves generalization of quantized networks.

title: A Convex Relaxation Barrier to Tight Robustness Verification of Neural Networks
summary: Unifies LP-relaxed verifiers under one convex relaxation framework with primal-dual strong duality, then solves the optimal relaxation exactly using over 22 CPU-years, finding it barely narrows the gap to PGD on MNIST and CIFAR networks: an inherent barrier.

title: Abstraction based Output Range Analysis for Neural Networks
summary: Computes output ranges of ReLU feed-forward networks by abstracting them into smaller interval neural networks with interval weights that over-approximate the output range, then solving a mixed integer linear program; experiments show the time-precision trade-off.

title: Beyond the Single Neuron Convex Barrier for Neural Network Certification
summary: k-ReLU computes convex relaxations of multiple ReLUs in a layer jointly rather than one at a time, overcoming the single-neuron triangle relaxation barrier; combined with existing verifiers, it certifies significantly more precisely while staying scalable.

title: Certifiable Robustness to Graph Perturbations
summary: The first method to certify robustness and non-robustness of graph neural networks and label/feature propagation to graph structure perturbations, computing certificates efficiently via connections to PageRank and Markov decision processes, plus robust training that increases certifiably robust nodes.

title: Certified Adversarial Robustness with Additive Noise
summary: Connects adversarial robustness to additive random noise to obtain scalable certified bounds on input perturbation norms, plus a training strategy that enlarges these bounds; on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet it competes with provable defense methods.

title: Certifying Geometric Robustness of Neural Networks
summary: DEEPG certifies robustness to geometric transformations such as rotation and scaling by computing sound, asymptotically optimal linear relaxations for any composition of transformations through sampling plus optimization, certifying more complex transformations than prior methods on large networks.

title: Computing Linear Restrictions of Neural Networks
summary: ExactLine exactly computes the restriction of a piecewise-linear network to a line segment, partitioning it into affine regions; used to find exact ACAS Xu decision boundaries, compute exact integrated gradients and test a hypothesis about adversarial examples.

title: Efficient and Accurate Estimation of Lipschitz Constants for Deep Neural Networks
summary: Computes guaranteed upper bounds on deep network Lipschitz constants via a semidefinite program, modelling activations as gradients of convex potentials with quadratic constraints; gives the most accurate bounds in experiments on random, MNIST and Iris networks, usable for robustness guarantees.

title: Neural Lyapunov Control
summary: Learns nonlinear control policies together with neural Lyapunov functions using a learner and a counterexample-finding falsifier, terminating with provable stability once no counterexample exists, and obtaining much larger regions of attraction than LQR and SOS/SDP.

title: On Relating Explanations and Adversarial Examples
summary: Shows that explanations and adversarial examples of ML models are related by a generalized hitting set duality, and gives algorithms that compute adversarial examples from explanations and vice versa.

title: Preventing Gradient Attenuation in Lipschitz Constrained Convolutional Networks
summary: Trains provably Lipschitz convolutional networks without gradient norm attenuation via BCOP, the Block Convolution Orthogonal Parameterization of orthogonal convolutions, competing with existing approaches for provable adversarial robustness and Wasserstein distance estimation.

title: Provable Certificates for Adversarial Examples: Fitting a Ball in the Union of Polytopes
summary: GeoCert computes exact pointwise robustness of ReLU networks for convex ℓp norms by finding the largest ball around an input inside a polyhedral complex, returning anytime lower bounds that tighten until exact and beat prior work under time limits.

title: Provably Robust Deep Learning via Adversarially Trained Smoothed Classifiers
summary: Improves randomized smoothing by adversarially training smoothed classifiers with an attack adapted to them, outperforming all existing provably ℓ2-robust classifiers on ImageNet and CIFAR-10; pre-training and semi-supervised learning give further gains.

title: Theoretical evidence for adversarial robustness through randomization
summary: Gives theoretical grounding for noise-injection defenses: relates the randomization rate to adversarial robustness for exponential-family noise distributions and derives an upper bound on the adversarial generalization gap of randomized networks, supported by experiments.

title: Tight Certificates of Adversarial Robustness for Randomly Smoothed Classifiers
summary: Extends robustness certificates for randomly smoothed classifiers beyond Gaussian ℓ2 to broad distribution classes, including discrete ℓ0-bounded adversaries, and tightens guarantees using function-class assumptions such as decision trees; evaluated on image and molecule datasets.

title: Property Inference for Deep Neural Networks
summary: Infers formal properties of feed-forward networks from neuron activation patterns, extracting input and layer preconditions that imply output properties; applied to MNIST and ACAS Xu networks for explanation, robustness guarantees, proof simplification and distillation.

title: Quantitative Verification of Neural Networks and Its Security Applications
summary: NPAQ quantitatively verifies binarized neural networks by estimating how many inputs satisfy a logical property with PAC-style soundness guarantees, applied to quantifying adversarial robustness, trojan attack efficacy and fairness.

title: Scalable Verified Training for Provably Robust Image Classification
summary: Shows that interval bound propagation, with a suitable loss and hyper-parameter schedule, trains large provably robust image classifiers that beat more complex methods on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and SVHN in verified accuracy, and verifies the largest model yet on downscaled ImageNet.

title: Counterexample-Guided Strategy Improvement for POMDPs Using Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Synthesizes POMDP strategies that provably satisfy temporal logic constraints by training an RNN, restricting it to a finite-memory strategy, verifying the induced Markov chain and retraining from counterexamples, improving the state of the art by up to three orders of magnitude in solving time and model size.

title: Heterogeneous Gaussian Mechanism: Preserving Differential Privacy in Deep Learning with Provable Robustness
summary: Preserves differential privacy in deep networks with a Heterogeneous Gaussian Mechanism that relaxes the privacy budget constraint to (0, ∞) and allows arbitrary noise redistribution; injecting this noise into the first hidden layer yields a tighter provable robustness bound against adversarial examples.

title: Robustra: Training Provable Robust Neural Networks over Reference Adversarial Space
summary: Robustra trains provably robust DNNs by solving the attacker-defender min-max game over a reference model's adversarial space through a linearized dual. On MNIST it cuts the ℓ∞ provable error bound from 2.74% to 2.09% at ε=0.1 and 24.19% to 16.91% at ε=0.3.

title: Statistical Guarantees for the Robustness of Bayesian Neural Networks
summary: Defines probabilistic robustness for Bayesian neural networks as the probability that an adversarial point exists in a bounded set, and estimates it with a priori error and confidence bounds using statistical verification, comparing approximate inference techniques on MNIST and a two-class subset of GTSRB.

title: Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing
summary: Proves a tight ℓ2 robustness guarantee for randomized smoothing with Gaussian noise, turning any noise-tolerant classifier into a certifiably robust one; reaches 49% certified top-1 accuracy on ImageNet for ℓ2 perturbations below 0.5.

title: On Certifying Non-Uniform Bounds against Adversarial Attacks
POPQORN: Quantifying Robustness of Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: POPQORN computes certified lower bounds on the minimum adversarial perturbation for recurrent networks, including vanilla RNNs, LSTMs and GRUs, handling multi-step inputs and gate-state interactions; per-step robustness quantification gives new insights.

title: PROVEN: Verifying Robustness of Neural Networks with a Probabilistic Approach
The Marabou Framework for Verification and Analysis of Deep Neural Networks
summary: Marabou is an SMT-based framework that verifies deep neural network properties by turning queries into constraint satisfaction problems, supporting various activations and topologies, high-level reasoning to prune search, parallel execution and TensorFlow inputs.

title: Knowing When to Stop: Evaluation and Verification of Conformity to Output-Size Specifications
summary: Studies attacks that lengthen outputs of variable-length models, using a differentiable proxy to find inputs giving outputs 50 times longer, and a verification method that proves output length stays below a bound for machine translation and image captioning models.

title: Robustness Verification of Classification Deep Neural Networks via Linear Programming
summary: Verifies robustness of classification networks with sigmoid activations by recasting it as checking the most suspected input point, a nonlinear optimization relaxed into a linear program; experiments show better precision and scalability on image classifiers.

title: An inductive synthesis framework for verifiable reinforcement learning
summary: Verifies reinforcement learning neural policies by synthesizing simpler deterministic programs plus inductive invariants through counterexample- and syntax-guided synthesis; the programs monitor the network at runtime and block unsafe actions, with low overhead across cyber-physical applications.

title: Optimization and abstraction: a synergistic approach for analyzing neural network robustness
summary: Charon verifies local robustness of neural networks by combining gradient-based counterexample search with abstraction-based proof search guided by a learned verification policy, giving a sound and δ-complete procedure that outperforms AI^2, Reluplex and Reluval.

title: A Statistical Approach to Assessing Neural Network Robustness
summary: Estimates the probability that a network property is violated under an input model with multi-level splitting, a Monte Carlo rare-event method, giving statistical robustness estimates that emulate formal verification on benchmarks while scaling to larger networks.

title: Boosting Robustness Certification of Neural Networks
Evaluating Robustness of Neural Networks with Mixed Integer Programming
summary: Formulates verification of piecewise-linear networks as a mixed integer program with tight formulations and a presolve step, running two to three orders of magnitude faster and finding the exact adversarial accuracy of an MNIST classifier at ℓ∞ ε=0.1.

title: Training for Faster Adversarial Robustness Verification via Inducing ReLU Stability
summary: Trains networks to be both robust and easier to verify by encouraging weight sparsity and ReLU stability; sparsity makes intractable verification tractable, and ReLU stability adds a 4-13x verification speedup across training procedures and verifiers.

title: Verification of Non-Linear Specifications for Neural Networks
summary: Extends neural network verification to convex-relaxable nonlinear specifications, such as energy conservation in learned dynamics, semantic label consistency under perturbation and bounded errors when summing handwritten digits, and verifies them effectively while exposing failure modes.

title: Certified Robustness to Adversarial Examples with Differential Privacy
summary: PixelDP certifies robustness to norm-bounded adversarial examples using a connection to differential privacy, the first certified defense that scales to large networks and datasets such as Inception on ImageNet and applies to arbitrary model types.

title: An abstract domain for certifying neural networks
summary: DeepPoly certifies deep neural networks with an abstract domain combining floating-point polyhedra and intervals, with transformers for affine, ReLU, sigmoid, tanh and maxpool; more precise than prior work, and with trace partitioning it proves robustness to rotations.

title: Abduction-Based Explanations for Machine Learning Models
summary: Computes cardinality- or subset-minimal explanations for any ML model by abductive reasoning, requiring only that the model be encoded as constraints decidable by an oracle; experiments on well-known datasets show the approach scales and produces high-quality explanations.

title: CNN-Cert: An Efficient Framework for Certifying Robustness of Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Certifies robustness of general convolutional networks with CNN-Cert, handling convolution, max-pooling, batch normalization, residual blocks and general activations, and generalizing Fast-Lin and CROWN; it is up to 17 and 11 times faster than those and 366 times faster than dual LP with similar or better bounds.

title: Inverse Abstraction of Neural Networks Using Symbolic Interpolation
summary: Computes compact symbolic over- and under-approximations of neural network pre-images layer by layer via symbolic interpolation, enabling formal analysis, extraction of simple control laws and interpretable descriptions of inputs leading to unsafe outputs.

title: RecurJac: An Efficient Recursive Algorithm for Bounding Jacobian Matrix of Neural Networks and Its Applications
summary: Computes upper and lower bounds on every element of a network's input Jacobian with the recursive RecurJac algorithm for a wide range of activations, yielding better local Lipschitz constants for robustness verification in polynomial time and characterizing the loss landscape, such as whether stationary points exist nearby.

title: Verification of RNN-Based Neural Agent-Environment Systems
summary: Verifies agent-environment systems whose stateful agent runs a ReLU recurrent network, using equivalences between recurrent and feed-forward networks on bounded traces to give a sound and complete procedure for properties in a simplified bounded LTL.

title: A Unified View of Piecewise Linear Neural Network Verification
summary: Presents a unified framework covering existing piecewise-linear network verifiers, yielding new combined methods with a two-orders-of-magnitude speedup, and a benchmark dataset used for the first experimental comparison of verification algorithms and problem hardness factors.

title: Efficient Formal Safety Analysis of Neural Networks
summary: Checks safety properties of neural networks, such as L-norm robustness, by estimating tight output bounds over input ranges and finding concrete counterexamples, outperforming existing approaches by orders of magnitude on networks 10 times larger.

title: Efficient Neural Network Robustness Certification with General Activation Functions
summary: CROWN certifies robustness of networks with general activations, including ReLU, tanh, sigmoid and arctan, by bounding activations with adaptively chosen linear and quadratic functions, improving certified lower bounds over Fast-Lin on ReLU networks at similar cost.

title: Fast and Effective Robustness Certification
summary: DeepZ certifies neural network robustness with abstract interpretation sound under floating point, supporting ReLU, tanh and sigmoid in feedforward and convolutional networks; it verifies 97% on an 88,500-unit network under L∞ ε=0.1 in 133 seconds average.

title: Lipschitz regularity of deep neural networks: analysis and efficient estimation
summary: Shows exact Lipschitz constant computation is NP-hard even for two-layer networks, then gives AutoLip, a generic upper bound for any automatically differentiable function, and SeqLip, which tightens bounds for sequential networks by splitting per layer pair.

title: Lipschitz-Margin Training: Scalable Certification of Perturbation Invariance for Deep Neural Networks
summary: Lower-bounds the adversarial perturbation size needed to fool a network using Lipschitz constants and prediction margins, applicable to complicated architectures, plus Lipschitz-margin training that enlarges provably guarded areas, giving non-trivial guarantees on large networks.

title: Scaling provable adversarial defenses
summary: Scales provable adversarial training to general networks with skip connections and nonlinearities, using random projections and cascades; provable robust error falls from 5.8% to 3.1% on MNIST at ε=0.1 and from 80% to 36.4% on CIFAR at ε=2/255.

title: Semidefinite relaxations for certifying robustness to adversarial examples
summary: Certifies robustness of arbitrary ReLU networks to adversarial examples with a semidefinite relaxation that is tighter than previous relaxations and gives meaningful guarantees on three networks not trained against it.

title: Formal Security Analysis of Neural Networks using Symbolic Intervals
summary: ReluVal checks security properties of ReLU networks without SMT solvers, using parallelizable symbolic interval analysis to bound outputs. It is 200 times faster than Reluplex on average and verifies a property on which Reluplex timed out.

title: Differentiable Abstract Interpretation for Provably Robust Neural Networks
summary: Trains large neural networks that are certifiably robust to adversarial perturbations by making abstract interpretation differentiable, with several abstract transformers that balance efficiency and precision.

title: Provable Defenses against Adversarial Examples via the Convex Outer Adversarial Polytope
summary: Trains ReLU classifiers provably robust to norm-bounded perturbations by minimizing worst-case loss over a convex outer approximation of reachable activations, solving the dual LP as a backprop-like network; on MNIST, provable error stays below 5.8% at ℓ∞ ε=0.1.

title: Towards Fast Computation of Certified Robustness for ReLU Networks
summary: Fast-Lin and Fast-Lip certify lower bounds on the minimum adversarial distortion of ReLU networks by linear bounding of ReLUs or local Lipschitz bounds, running over 10,000 times faster than Reluplex, and prove approximation hardness for ℓ1 distortion.

title: Reachability Analysis of Deep Neural Networks with Provable Guarantees
summary: Computes lower and upper bounds of a Lipschitz-continuous function over a DNN's outputs for a set of inputs using adaptive nested optimisation, which covers safety verification, output range analysis and robustness measurement, and handles a broader class of networks than prior verifiers efficiently.

title: Certified Defenses against Adversarial Examples
summary: Certifies one-hidden-layer networks against adversarial attacks via a differentiable semidefinite relaxation bound that is also optimized during training; on MNIST the resulting certificate guarantees no attack within ε=0.1 per pixel exceeds 35% test error.

title: Certifying Some Distributional Robustness with Principled Adversarial Training
summary: Trains models with distributionally robust optimization over a Wasserstein ball via a Lagrangian penalty, augmenting updates with worst-case data perturbations; for smooth losses this provably gives moderate robustness and certifies robustness of the population loss at low cost.

Safe Reinforcement Learning via Formal Methods: Toward Safe Control Through Proof and Learning
summary: Ensures safe reinforcement learning by combining formal verification with verified runtime monitoring: safety guarantees hold while the agent explores within verified control choices, and on model violations it learns to return to modelled states; demonstrated on adaptive cruise control.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding
summary: Learns optimal reinforcement learning policies while enforcing temporal logic safety specifications with a synthesized shield that either restricts the agent to safe actions before it decides or corrects unsafe actions after, gives conditions to preserve learning convergence, and demonstrates it on several challenging scenarios.

title: Verifying Properties of Binarized Deep Neural Networks
summary: Verifies properties of binarized neural networks, especially adversarial robustness, by encoding them exactly as Boolean formulas and using modern SAT solvers with a counterexample-guided search, scaling to medium-size image classification networks.

title: Formal Guarantees on the Robustness of a Classifier against Adversarial Manipulation
summary: Gives the first formal instance-specific lower bounds on the input change needed to alter a classifier's decision, and proposes Cross-Lipschitz regularization that improves robustness of kernel methods and neural networks without loss in prediction performance.

title: Safe Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Stability Guarantees
summary: Learns neural network control policies with provable Lyapunov stability certificates using statistical dynamics models with a Gaussian process prior, safely expanding the safe region; optimizes a policy on a simulated inverted pendulum without it ever falling.

title: FairSquare: probabilistic verification of program fairness
summary: FairSquare automatically certifies that decision-making programs meet fairness definitions, encoded as probabilistic program properties, using a new technique for verifying probabilistic properties; it verifies fairness for programs beyond reach of existing program analysis tools.

title: Reluplex: An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks
summary: Reluplex verifies properties of deep ReLU networks, or finds counterexamples, by extending the simplex method to handle the non-convex ReLU; on ACAS Xu collision-avoidance networks it proves properties of networks an order of magnitude larger than before.

title: Safety Verification of Deep Neural Networks
summary: Verifies safety of feed-forward image classifiers with an SMT-based framework that discretizes a neighbourhood of an input under manipulations such as scratches, camera angle or lighting, and propagates the analysis layer by layer, guaranteeing to find adversarial examples if any exist; implemented with Z3.

On Collective Robustness of Bagging Against Data Poisoning
summary: Certifies general bagging collectively against global data poisoning by solving a binary integer linear program for the maximum number of simultaneously changed predictions, bounds the tolerable poison budget for vanilla bagging, and proposes hash bagging, a deterministic hash-based subsampling that improves robustness almost for free.
